reconcile.note: Clarke reads 'confusion' in 1 Corinthians 14:33 as the specific disorder of chaotic simultaneous speech in worship, not a blanket denial that God ever causes any confusion.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible treats Genesis 11's language-confounding and 1 Corinthians 1:27's confounding of the wise as directly contradicting Paul's claim that God is not a God of confusion.

sides.snippet: the name of it was called Babel, because Yahweh confused the language of all the earth, there
sides.verseText: Therefore the name of it was called Babel, because Yahweh confused the language of all the earth, there. From there, Yahweh scattered them abroad on the surface of all the earth.

sides.snippet: for God is not a God of confusion, but of peace.
